The Muslim commander, Khalid ibn al-Walid, defeated the Byzantine commander, Chorasmes, and captured the fortified city of Asyaf. The battle took place near the Jordan River.

Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab al-Ashraf' mentions that during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD), the Muslim commander, Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, was appointed as the governor of Syria. Muawiya's forces captured the city of Asyaf, which was located near the Jordan River, from the Byzantines. The capture of Asyaf provided the Muslims with a strategic position against future Byzantine attacks.
